### Summary

This PR adds support for parsing task status from the raw text input. Tasks can now include a `[status]` marker that is extracted and stored as part of the task object.

---

### What's Added

- New function `extract_status(task_str: str) -> Tuple[str, Optional[str]]`  
  Extracts: `[todo]`,  `[inProgress]`, or  `[done]`, tags from task names.
  Defaults to `None` if no status is present.

- Updated `parse_input_data()` logic:
  - Uses `extract_status()` to detect status for each task
  - Ensures both parent and child tasks retain correct status
  - Builds task dictionaries with `task`, `depends_on`, and `status` fields

- Updated docstrings and type hints to reflect `Optional[str]` status handling

---

```text
Task A [done] -> Task B [todo]
Task C

This commit introduces a new document, COMPREHENSIVE_ENGINEERING_ROADMAP.md, which details a strategic engineering roadmap for Wire.

The roadmap aims to guide Wire's development into a production-ready, best-in-class streaming platform, with specific goals to outperform Apache Flink in areas like developer experience, operational simplicity, and certain performance niches.

It includes:
- Current state analysis and gap identification.
- Short-term (0-4 months), mid-term (4-9 months), and long-term (9+ months) prioritized goals with technical rationale.
- Actionable recommendations for development workflows, scalability, community adoption, and achieving high-throughput, fault-tolerant streaming.

* Added a new API endpoint `/portfolios/` to list all portfolios with their details, including associated services. (`apps/interface_adapters/api/v1/urls.py`, [apps/interface_adapters/api/v1/urls.pyL17-R19](diffhunk://#diff-5f919806e790c298ef7f1ce0c30b8755395eb795e420d331f84ad3ad675faaf1L17-R19))

   --------------------------

- The "no-ctracer" warning is not issued for Python pre-release versions.
  Coverage doesn't ship compiled wheels for those versions, so this was far too
  noisy.

- On Python 3.14+, the "sysmon" core is now the default if it's supported for
  your configuration.  Plugins and dynamic contexts are still not supported
  with it.


.. _changes_7-9-0:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.9.0
   ```
   --------------------------

- Added a ``[run] core`` configuration setting to specify the measurement core,
  which was previously only available through the COVERAGE_CORE environment
  variable. Finishes `issue 1746`_.

- Fixed incorrect rendering of f-strings with doubled braces, closing `issue
  1980`_.

- If the C tracer core can't be imported, a warning ("no-ctracer") is issued
  with the reason.

- The C tracer core extension module now conforms to `PEP 489`_, closing `issue
  1977`_.  Thanks, `Adam Turner <pull 1978_>`_.

- Fixed a "ValueError: min() arg is an empty sequence" error caused by strange
  empty modules, found by `oss-fuzz`_.

.. _issue 1746: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1746
.. _issue 1977: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1977

.. _changes_7-8-2:

   ### 7.8.2

  Thanks, `Finn Womack <pull 1972_>`_.

.. _changes_7-8-1:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.8.1
   ```
   --------------------------

- A number of EncodingWarnings were fixed that could appear if you've enabled
  PYTHONWARNDEFAULTENCODING, fixing `issue 1966`_.  Thanks, `Henry Schreiner
  <pull 1967_>`_.

- Fixed a race condition when using sys.monitoring with free-threading Python,
  closing `issue 1970`_.

.. _issue 1966: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1966
.. _pull 1967: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1967
.. _issue 1970: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1970

.. _changes_7-8-0:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.8.0
   ```
   --------------------------

- Added a new ``source_dirs`` setting for symmetry with the existing
  ``source_pkgs`` setting. It's preferable to the existing ``source`` setting,
  because you'll get a clear error when directories don't exist. Fixes `issue
  1942`_.  Thanks, `Jeremy Fleischman <pull 1943_>`_.

- Fix: the PYTHONSAFEPATH environment variable new in Python 3.11 is properly
  supported, closing `issue 1696`_.  Thanks, `Philipp A. <pull 1700_>`_.  This
  works properly except for a detail when using the ``coverage`` command on
  Windows.  There you can use ``python -m coverage`` instead if you need exact
  emulation.

.. _issue 1696: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1696

  test!


.. _changes_7-7-0:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.7.0
   ```
   --------------------------

- The Coverage object has a new method, :meth:`.Coverage.branch_stats` for
  getting simple branch information for a module.  Closes `issue 1888`_.

- The :class:`Coverage constructor<.Coverage>` now has a ``plugins`` parameter
  for passing in plugin objects directly, thanks to `Alex Gaynor <pull
  1919_>`_.

- Many constant tests in if statements are now recognized as being optimized
  away.  For example, previously ``if 13:`` would have been considered a branch
  with one path not taken.  Now it is understood as always true and no coverage
  is missing.

- The experimental sys.monitoring support now works for branch coverage if you
  are using Python 3.14.0 alpha 6 or newer.  This should reduce the overhead
  coverage.py imposes on your test suite. Set the environment variable
  ``COVERAGE_CORE=sysmon`` to try it out.

- Confirmed support for PyPy 3.11. Thanks Michał Górny.

# Major Platform Modernization: Google AI SDK Migration + LLM Cost Optimization + Critical Bug Fixes


## Overview
This PR represents a comprehensive platform modernization encompassing AI infrastructure upgrades, cost optimization strategies, and critical user experience fixes. The changes span backend AI services, cost management, data integrity, and frontend user flows.

## 🚀 Major Infrastructure Upgrades
Google AI SDK Migration
Migrated from deprecated google-generativeai to unified google-genai SDK for future compatibility
Upgraded to Gemini 2.5 Flash with enhanced reasoning capabilities via 1024-token thinking budget
Centralized model configuration through ModelConfig class eliminating hardcoded model names
Updated all LLM service imports and API calls to new unified client architecture
Enhanced error handling and streaming support with new SDK patterns
Dual-Model LLM Cost Optimization
Implemented factory pattern (LLMServiceFactory) for automatic model selection based on task complexity
Introduced Gemini Flash Lite for simple processing tasks (71% of operations)
Preserved Gemini Flash for complex reasoning tasks (29% of operations)
Achieved ~50% cost reduction while maintaining quality for creative tasks
Updated 6/8 LLM processes to use cost-optimized Flash Lite model
Cost Optimization Breakdown:

Flash Lite (71%): Summary generation, paragraph formatting, character processing, image prompts
Flash (29%): Story generation, complex image scene generation
## 🔧 Critical Data Integrity Fixes
Summary Screen Data Corruption Resolution
Identified and removed problematic state modification functions that were corrupting adventure data
Fixed localStorage corruption that was overwriting good database state
Resolved WebSocket timeout fallback issues that caused state corruption
Implemented read-only state reconstruction to prevent modification during display
Added comprehensive logging for debugging complex state management issues
Chapter Counting Backend Consistency
Fixed "Chapters Completed: 11" display error showing incorrect count instead of 10
Standardized SUMMARY chapter filtering across all backend counting methods
Resolved inconsistencies between AdventureStateManager and SummaryService implementations
Updated error fallback cases to use consistent filtered chapter counts
## 🎨 User Experience Improvements
Summary Page Navigation Fixes
Resolved "dead end" summary page where users couldn't start new adventures
Fixed non-functional "Start New Adventure" button (was text-only, now clickable)
Completely removed "Return Home" button using proper DOM removal
Fixed auto-resumption bypass that was skipping carousel selection
Added localStorage clearing to ensure fresh adventure start experience
## 📁 Files Changed (30 files total)
AI Infrastructure:

requirements.txt - SDK version upgrades
app/services/llm/ - Complete LLM service modernization
app/services/image_generation_service.py - Unified SDK integration
tests/simulations/generate_chapter_summaries.py - Updated for new architecture
Data Management:

app/services/adventure_state_manager.py - State consistency fixes
app/services/summary/ - Chapter counting and corruption fixes
app/services/state_storage_service.py - Data integrity improvements
Frontend:

app/static/summary-chapter/react-app-patch.js - Button functionality fixes
app/static/js/ - UI state management improvements
Documentation:

memory-bank/ - Updated with latest architecture and fixes
## 🧪 Testing & Validation
✅ Cost optimization validated through three parallel sub-agents
✅ Summary data corruption resolved with live testing
✅ Button functionality restored with proper navigation flow
✅ SDK migration verified with full adventure completion testing
✅ Chapter counting accuracy confirmed across all display contexts
💰 Business Impact
~50% reduction in LLM costs through strategic model selection
Enhanced platform stability with modern Google AI SDK
Improved user retention by fixing summary page navigation dead end
Data accuracy restoration eliminating confusing chapter count displays
Future-proofed AI infrastructure for upcoming Google AI features
## 🔄 Architecture Improvements
Factory pattern implementation for scalable LLM service management
Centralized configuration management for better maintainability
Read-only data reconstruction preventing state corruption
Enhanced error handling across AI service layer
Comprehensive debugging infrastructure for complex state issues
This PR transforms the platform's AI infrastructure while resolving critical user-facing issues, positioning the application for improved cost efficiency and enhanced user experience.

author: andriydruk
body:
### Motivation

Starting with Android 11, the platform ships its time-zone package as `com.google.android.tzdata2`, whose files use the TZif v2/v3 specification ([RFC 8536](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8536)) with 64-bit transition timestamps (Google also introduced a new APEX-based mechanism for updating time zones on all Android 10+ devices)
https://source.android.com/docs/core/ota/modular-system/timezone

`CFTimeZone.c` currently only understands v1 layout, so CoreFoundation on Android silently falls back to “GMT” for any device that only contains the new format

### What this patch does
* Adds support for the new APEX tzdata path
* Extends `struct tzhead` to include the one-byte `version` field
* Introduces `__CFDetzcode64` to decode 64-bit big-endian integers safely (no UB on signed shifts)
* During parsing  
  * read the first header, determine `version`, and set `trans_size` to `4` (v1) or `8` (v2+)
  * if `version > 1`, skip the v1 data block and read the second header that precedes the 64-bit section
  * use `trans_size` consistently when advancing the transition and type pointers
* For TZif v1 files, the parsing path is identical to the original implementation

### Testing
This patch affects CFTimeZone in CoreFoundation only. It does not affect Foundation.TimeZone, which continues to use ICU-based time zone data:
* APEX tzdata version on Android device: 2025b
* Swift Foundation (ICU) tzdata version: 2023c

I wrote a test case verifying the recent time zone change in Asia/Almaty, where Kazakhstan unified to UTC+5 in March 2024. However, I didn't commit it, as it would fail on all platforms using older tzdata (e.g. ICU 2023c).

```
    /// Kazakhstan unified on UTC +5 at 00:00 local, 1 March 2024.
    /// After that moment Asia/Almaty should report +05:00.
    /// ICU/tzdata 2023c still returns +06:00, so the
    /// assertion below fails on tzdata before 2024a+.
    func testAsiaAlmatyOffsetAfter2024Change() {
        guard let almaty = TimeZone(identifier: "Asia/Almaty") else {
            XCTFail("Asia/Almaty not found")
            return
        }

        // Local time 2024-06-01 12:00 in Almaty
        var comps = DateComponents()
        comps.year = 2024
        comps.month = 6
        comps.day = 1
        comps.hour = 12
        comps.timeZone = almaty

        let calendar = Calendar(identifier: .gregorian)
        let date = calendar.date(from: comps)!

        // Expected offset (UTC+5) after the March 2024 change
        let expectedSeconds = 5 * 3_600
        XCTAssertEqual(almaty.secondsFromGMT(for: date), expectedSeconds)
    }

    func testAsiaAlmatyOffsetAfter2024ChangeCF() {
        guard let timeZoneName = CFStringCreateWithCString(nil, "Asia/Almaty", CFStringBuiltInEncodings.UTF8.rawValue),
              let almaty = CFTimeZoneCreateWithName(nil, timeZoneName, false) else {
            XCTFail("Asia/Almaty not found")
            return
        }
        
        var gregorianDate = CFGregorianDate(
            year: 2024,
            month: 6,
            day: 1,
            hour: 12,
            minute: 0,
            second: 0.0
        )
        
        let absoluteTime = CFGregorianDateGetAbsoluteTime(gregorianDate, almaty)
        let offsetSeconds = CFTimeZoneGetSecondsFromGMT(almaty, absoluteTime)
        
        // Expected offset (UTC+5) after the March 2024 change
        let expectedSeconds: CFTimeInterval = 5 * 3_600
        XCTAssertEqual(offsetSeconds, expectedSeconds)
    }
```

Result on Android with tzdata 2025b
❌ Foundation.TimeZone still returns outdated UTC+6 due to bundled ICU 2023c
✅ CFTimeZone reports correct offset (UTC+5)
```
Test Case 'TestTimeZone.testAsiaAlmatyOffsetAfter2024Change' started at 2025-07-05 19:39:00.480
TestFoundation/TestTimeZone.swift:297: error: TestTimeZone.testAsiaAlmatyOffsetAfter2024Change : XCTAssertEqual failed: ("21600") is not equal to ("18000") - Asia/Almaty should be UTC+5 after 2024-03-01. If this assertion fails (got 6 h), the device is running tzdata 2023c or older.
Test Case 'TestTimeZone.testAsiaAlmatyOffsetAfter2024Change' failed (0.003 seconds)
Test Case 'TestTimeZone.testAsiaAlmatyOffsetAfter2024ChangeCF' started at 2025-07-05 19:39:00.483
Test Case 'TestTimeZone.testAsiaAlmatyOffsetAfter2024ChangeCF' passed (0.001 seconds)
```

### Next steps
Explore how to make Foundation.TimeZone use the system-provided tzdata on Android. Currently, it relies on ICU's bundled data, which may be outdated compared to the APEX module. Aligning both would ensure consistent and up-to-date time zone behavior across the system.

author: kemzeb
body:
Resolves #453.

Much harder than I expected to implement, but I think my logic and implementation checks out. The algorithm is the following:

- Take the _exclude_ set from CLI input and resolve it to actual nodes in the graph
- Determine all possible candidates for exclusion by performing DFS
  - So we add the direct and transitive dependencies of the exclude nodes we gathered in Step 1 into a `candidates` set, but **we aren't sure yet** if they should be excluded since a non-excluded node maybe using it. **This is the reason** why we have more steps below
- Create a reversed graph so that we know all the nodes that depend on a specific node
- Iterate over `candidates`, **counting** the number of dependents for each node using the reversed graph
- Now iterate over the explicitly-excluded nodes that we created in Step 1, where for each node:
  - Add it to the **new excluded set**
  - Iterate over their children. For each child, get the dependent count of that child and decrement it by 1
    - If the count equals 0, we haven't added it to the new set, and it isn't apart of the original resolved set created in Step 1, this child is a candidate for exclusion so let's add it (and in effect, also add their applicable children)
    - If this specific branch is never reached, it means that **their is a non-excluded node that has an outgoing edge to child**. We should not remove it
- Return the **new excluded set**, which will contain both the explicitly-excluded nodes and the dependency nodes associated to them

body: ## Problem The technology icons section in the README was experiencing layout instability due to the use of empty `` tags as spacers between icons. These empty img elements without `src` attributes are interpreted inconsistently by GitHub's markdown renderer, leading to unpredictable layout behavior where icons could suddenly fill the complete width of the page. ## Root Cause Empty `` tags without a `src` attribute cause layout instability because: - GitHub's markdown renderer handles them inconsistently - They create unpredictable spacing behavior - Browser interpretation varies for malformed img elements ## Solution Replaced all `` spacer elements with semantic CSS-based spacing using `margin-right: 12px` on the actual icon images. ### Before: ```html ``` ### After: ```html ``` ## Changes - ✅ Removed 13 empty `` spacer elements - ✅ Added `style="margin-right: 12px;"` to the first 13 icon images - ✅ Last icon (raspberrypi) has no right margin to prevent trailing space - ✅ Maintained exact same visual spacing (12px between icons) ## Benefits - **Stable rendering**: CSS margins are reliably interpreted across all browsers and GitHub's renderer - **Cleaner code**: Removed 13 redundant empty elements (-27 lines, +14 lines) - **Better semantics**: Icons are properly spaced with CSS instead of layout hacks - **Future-proof**: No dependency on GitHub's handling of malformed HTML elements ## Testing The visual appearance remains identical, but the underlying implementation is now stable and semantic. The 12px spacing between technology icons is preserved while eliminating the layout instability issue. --- 💡 You can make Copilot smarter by setting up custom instructions, customizing its development environment and configuring Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers. # 🏆 User Achievements Contract - PR Description

## 📋 Overview

This PR implements a comprehensive, permissionless Cairo smart contract for the Mediolano platform that enables recording, tracking, and showcasing user achievements and scores in a fully sovereign and trustless way.

## 🎯 Problem Statement

Mediolano needs a foundational identity layer that enables:
- **Proof of Creativity**: Verifiable on-chain achievement tracking
- **Merit-Based Recognition**: Transparent scoring and ranking systems
- **Community Building**: Leaderboards and social proof mechanisms
- **Creator Empowerment**: Showcase contributions without centralized validation

## ✅ Solution Implemented

### Core Features
- **Achievement Tracking System**: Record and store user achievements with metadata
- **Activity Event Processing**: Permissionless recording of user activities by Mediolano platform
- **Badge Management System**: Mint and manage achievement badges (9 types)
- **Certificate Management System**: Issue and track certificates with optional expiry dates (7 types)
- **Leaderboard & Ranking System**: On-chain ranking based on user points
- **Configurable Point System**: Weighted scoring for different activity types
- **Pagination Support**: Efficient querying for large datasets
- **Event Emission**: Comprehensive events for indexing and real-time updates

### Technical Architecture
```
User Achievements Contract
├── Achievement Tracking System
├── Activity Event Processing
├── Badge Management System
├── Certificate Management System
├── Leaderboard & Ranking System
├── Point System with Configurable Weights
└── Access Control & Owner Management
```

## 🔧 Technical Implementation

### Contract Structure
- **710 lines** of Cairo 1.0+ code
- **15 core functions** implemented
- **4 data structures** defined
- **9 achievement types** supported
- **9 activity types** supported
- **9 badge types** supported
- **7 certificate types** supported
- **7 event types** for indexing

### Key Data Structures
```cairo
struct Achievement {
    achievement_type: AchievementType,
    timestamp: u64,
    metadata_id: felt252,
    asset_id: Option<felt252>,
    category: Option<felt252>,
    points: u32,
}

struct Badge {
    badge_type: BadgeType,
    timestamp: u64,
    metadata_id: felt252,
    is_active: bool,
}

struct Certificate {
    certificate_type: CertificateType,
    timestamp: u64,
    metadata_id: felt252,
    expiry_date: Option<u64>,
    is_valid: bool,
}

struct LeaderboardEntry {
    user: ContractAddress,
    total_points: u32,
    achievements_count: u32,
    badges_count: u32,
    certificates_count: u32,
}
```

### Storage Optimization
Fixed critical storage issue with proper ID mapping:
```cairo
// Before: Map<ActivityType, u32> (not supported)
// After: Map<u32, u32> with helper function
activity_points: Map<u32, u32>, // Maps activity_type_id to points

fn _activity_type_to_id(self: @ContractState, activity_type: ActivityType) -> u32 {
    match activity_type {
        ActivityType::AssetMinted => 0,
        ActivityType::AssetSold => 1,
        // ... etc
    }
}
```

## 🧪 Testing Implementation

### Test Coverage
- **509 lines** of comprehensive test code
- **15 test functions** covering all functionality
- **Owner permission handling** properly implemented
- **Modern Cairo syntax** used throughout
- **Comprehensive assertions** for validation

### Test Functions
1. **Core Functionality**: Constructor, achievement recording, activity events, badges, certificates
2. **Advanced Features**: Leaderboard, pagination, multiple achievements, activity points
3. **Type Coverage**: All achievement, badge, certificate, and activity types
4. **Management**: Owner management, comprehensive user profiles

### Test Improvements
- ✅ Fixed owner permission issues with proper contract deployment
- ✅ Updated constructor calls with owner parameter
- ✅ Modernized loop syntax to use `while` loops
- ✅ Added comprehensive assertion checking
- ✅ Implemented proper cheat functions for testing

## 📊 Features Supported

### Achievement Types
- **Mint**: Asset creation achievements
- **Sale**: Sales and marketplace achievements
- **License**: Licensing and IP achievements
- **Transfer**: Asset transfer achievements
- **Collection**: Collection creation achievements
- **Collaboration**: Collaborative work achievements
- **Innovation**: Innovation and creativity achievements
- **Community**: Community contribution achievements
- **Custom**: Custom achievement types

### Activity Types
- **AssetMinted**: When a user mints an asset
- **AssetSold**: When a user sells an asset
- **AssetLicensed**: When a user licenses an asset
- **AssetTransferred**: When a user transfers an asset
- **CollectionCreated**: When a user creates a collection
- **CollaborationJoined**: When a user joins a collaboration
- **InnovationAwarded**: When a user receives innovation recognition
- **CommunityContribution**: When a user contributes to the community
- **CustomActivity**: Custom activity types

### Badge Types
- **Creator**: For asset creators
- **Seller**: For successful sellers
- **Licensor**: For IP licensors
- **Collector**: For asset collectors
- **Innovator**: For innovative creators
- **CommunityLeader**: For community leaders
- **EarlyAdopter**: For early platform adopters
- **TopPerformer**: For top-performing users
- **CustomBadge**: Custom badge types

### Certificate Types
- **CreatorCertificate**: Certifies asset creation skills
- **SellerCertificate**: Certifies sales achievements
- **LicensorCertificate**: Certifies licensing expertise
- **InnovationCertificate**: Certifies innovation contributions
- **CommunityCertificate**: Certifies community involvement
- **AchievementCertificate**: General achievement certification
- **CustomCertificate**: Custom certificate types

## 🔐 Access Control

### Owner Functions (Mediolano Platform)
- `record_achievement()`: Record new achievements
- `record_activity_event()`: Record activity events
- `mint_badge()`: Mint achievement badges
- `mint_certificate()`: Issue certificates
- `set_activity_points()`: Configure point weights
- `set_owner()`: Transfer ownership

### Public Functions
- `get_user_achievements()`: Query user achievements
- `get_user_total_points()`: Get user points
- `get_user_badges()`: Get user badges
- `get_user_certificates()`: Get user certificates
- `get_leaderboard()`: View leaderboard
- `get_user_rank()`: Get user rank

## 📈 Events Emitted

The contract emits comprehensive events for indexing:
- `AchievementRecorded`: When a new achievement is recorded
- `ActivityEventRecorded`: When an activity event is recorded
- `BadgeMinted`: When a new badge is minted
- `CertificateMinted`: When a new certificate is minted
- `PointsUpdated`: When user points are updated
- `LeaderboardUpdated`: When the leaderboard is updated
- `OwnerChanged`: When ownership is transferred

## 🚀 Integration Ready

### Frontend Integration
```typescript
// Example frontend integration
const achievements = await contract.get_user_achievements(userAddress, 0, 10);
const totalPoints = await contract.get_user_total_points(userAddress);
const rank = await contract.get_user_rank(userAddress);
const leaderboard = await contract.get_leaderboard(0, 20);
```

### Backend Integration
```typescript
// Example backend integration for recording achievements
await contract.record_achievement(
    userAddress,
    'Mint', // AchievementType
    ipfsMetadataHash,
    assetId,
    category,
    points
);
```

- `contracts/User-Achievements/Scarb.toml` - Proj

author: andoriyaprashant
body:
## Summary

- Fixes an accessibility issue where sidebar items (like Maps, Workloads, Storage etc) were still reachable using the Tab key even when the sidebar was visually closed.

## Related Issue

Related:
- #245 

## Changes

- Now, when the sidebar is closed:
  - Sidebar items are hidden from keyboard navigation by applying `tabIndex={-1}`.
  - The sidebar container is hidden from screen readers using `aria-hidden="true"`.
- Sidebar items become focusable again when the sidebar is reopened.

## Steps to Test

1. Navigate to the Headlamp app in your browser.
2. Close the sidebar using the shrink sidebar button.
3. Press the Tab key repeatedly and observe:
    - Sidebar items like Maps, Workloads, Storage, etc. are no longer focusable.
    - The keyboard focus skips directly to the next visible element (like the main content).
4. Click the Headlamp logo again to reopen the sidebar.
5. Press the Tab key again and verify:
    - Sidebar items are now focusable as expected.

author: st0012
body:
ZJIT already can generate guard type instructions for *Exact types.

For example:

```
def test(strings)
  strings.map do |string|
    string.bytesize
  end
end

test(["foo", "bar"])
```

```
HIR:
fn block in test:
bb0(v0:BasicObject, v1:BasicObject):
  PatchPoint MethodRedefined(String@0x1014be890, bytesize@0x19f1)
  v7:StringExact = GuardType v1, StringExact
  v8:Fixnum = CCall bytesize@0x16fa4cc18, v7
  Return v8

```

But zjit only supported guarding fixnums so this script would panic.

This commit adds support for guarding *Exact types.

author: pyup-bot
body:
This PR updates [coverage](https://pypi.org/project/coverage) from **6.3.2** to **7.9.2**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 7.9.2
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: complex conditionals within a line might cause a KeyError when using
  sys.monitoring, as reported in `issue 1991`_.  This is now fixed.

- Fix: we can now measure coverage for code in Python archive (.par) files.
  Thanks, `Itamer Oren <pull 1984_>`_.

.. _pull 1984: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1984
.. _issue 1991: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1991


.. _changes_7-9-1:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.9.1
   ```
   --------------------------

- The "no-ctracer" warning is not issued for Python pre-release versions.
  Coverage doesn't ship compiled wheels for those versions, so this was far too
  noisy.

- On Python 3.14+, the "sysmon" core is now the default if it's supported for
  your configuration.  Plugins and dynamic contexts are still not supported
  with it.


.. _changes_7-9-0:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.9.0
   ```
   --------------------------

- Added a ``[run] core`` configuration setting to specify the measurement core,
  which was previously only available through the COVERAGE_CORE environment
  variable. Finishes `issue 1746`_.

- Fixed incorrect rendering of f-strings with doubled braces, closing `issue
  1980`_.

- If the C tracer core can't be imported, a warning ("no-ctracer") is issued
  with the reason.

- The C tracer core extension module now conforms to `PEP 489`_, closing `issue
  1977`_.  Thanks, `Adam Turner <pull 1978_>`_.

- Fixed a "ValueError: min() arg is an empty sequence" error caused by strange
  empty modules, found by `oss-fuzz`_.

.. _issue 1746: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1746
.. _issue 1977: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1977
.. _pull 1978: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1978
.. _issue 1980: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1980
.. _PEP 489: https://peps.python.org/pep-0489
.. _oss-fuzz: https://google.github.io/oss-fuzz/


.. _changes_7-8-2:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.8.2
   ```
   --------------------------

- Wheels are provided for Windows ARM64 on Python 3.11, 3.12, and 3.13.
  Thanks, `Finn Womack <pull 1972_>`_.

.. _issue 1971: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1971
.. _pull 1972: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1972

.. _changes_7-8-1:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.8.1
   ```
   --------------------------

- A number of EncodingWarnings were fixed that could appear if you've enabled
  PYTHONWARNDEFAULTENCODING, fixing `issue 1966`_.  Thanks, `Henry Schreiner
  <pull 1967_>`_.

- Fixed a race condition when using sys.monitoring with free-threading Python,
  closing `issue 1970`_.

.. _issue 1966: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1966
.. _pull 1967: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1967
.. _issue 1970: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1970

.. _changes_7-8-0:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.8.0
   ```
   --------------------------

- Added a new ``source_dirs`` setting for symmetry with the existing
  ``source_pkgs`` setting. It's preferable to the existing ``source`` setting,
  because you'll get a clear error when directories don't exist. Fixes `issue
  1942`_.  Thanks, `Jeremy Fleischman <pull 1943_>`_.

- Fix: the PYTHONSAFEPATH environment variable new in Python 3.11 is properly
  supported, closing `issue 1696`_.  Thanks, `Philipp A. <pull 1700_>`_.  This
  works properly except for a detail when using the ``coverage`` command on
  Windows.  There you can use ``python -m coverage`` instead if you need exact
  emulation.

.. _issue 1696: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1696
.. _pull 1700: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1700
.. _issue 1942: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1942
.. _pull 1943: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1943

.. _changes_7-7-1:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.7.1
   ```
   --------------------------

- A few small tweaks to the sys.monitoring support for Python 3.14.  Please
  test!


.. _changes_7-7-0:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.7.0
   ```
   --------------------------

- The Coverage object has a new method, :meth:`.Coverage.branch_stats` for
  getting simple branch information for a module.  Closes `issue 1888`_.

- The :class:`Coverage constructor<.Coverage>` now has a ``plugins`` parameter
  for passing in plugin objects directly, thanks to `Alex Gaynor <pull
  1919_>`_.

- Many constant tests in if statements are now recognized as being optimized
  away.  For example, previously ``if 13:`` would have been considered a branch
  with one path not taken.  Now it is understood as always true and no coverage
  is missing.

- The experimental sys.monitoring support now works for branch coverage if you
  are using Python 3.14.0 alpha 6 or newer.  This should reduce the overhead
  coverage.py imposes on your test suite. Set the environment variable
  ``COVERAGE_CORE=sysmon`` to try it out.

- Confirmed support for PyPy 3.11. Thanks Michał Górny.

.. _issue 1888: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1888
.. _pull 1919: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1919


.. _changes_7-6-12:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.12
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: some aarch64 distributions were missing (`issue 1927`_).  These are now
  building reliably.

.. _issue 1927: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1927

.. _changes_7-6-11:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.11
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: a memory leak in CTracer has been fixed.  The details are in `issue
  1924`_ and `pytest-dev 676`_.  This should reduce the memory footprint for
  everyone even if it hadn't caused a problem before.

- We now ship a py3-none-any.whl wheel file.  Thanks, `Russell Keith-Magee
  <pull 1914_>`_.

.. _pull 1914: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1914
.. _issue 1924: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1924
.. _pytest-dev 676: https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-cov/issues/676

.. _changes_7-6-10:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.10
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: some descriptions of missing branches in HTML and LCOV reports were
  incorrect when multi-line statements were involved (`issue 1874`_ and `issue
  1875`_).  These are now fixed.

- Fix: Python 3.14 `defers evaluation of annotations <pep649_>`_ by moving them
  into separate code objects.  That code is rarely executed, so coverage.py
  would mark them as missing, as reported in `issue 1908`_.  Now they are
  ignored by coverage automatically.

- Fixed an obscure and mysterious problem on PyPy 3.10 seemingly involving
  mocks, imports, and trace functions: `issue 1902`_.  To be honest, I don't
  understand the problem or the solution, but ``git bisect`` helped find it,
  and now it's fixed.

- Docs: re-wrote the :ref:`subprocess` page to put multiprocessing first and to
  highlight the correct use of :class:`multiprocessing.Pool
  <python:multiprocessing.pool.Pool>`.

.. _issue 1874: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1874
.. _issue 1875: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1875
.. _issue 1902: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1902
.. _issue 1908: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1908
.. _pep649: https://docs.python.org/3.14/whatsnew/3.14.html#whatsnew314-pep649


.. _changes_7-6-9:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.9
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: `Tomas Uribe fixed <pull 1901_>`_ a performance problem in the XML
  report.  Large code bases should produce XML reports much faster now.

.. _pull 1901: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1901


.. _changes_7-6-8:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.8
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: the LCOV report code assumed that a branch line that took no branches

author: terminallylazy
body:
Implement complete AG-UI (Agent User Interaction) protocol for dynamic UI generation and multi-agent collaboration in Agent Zero framework.

## Core Features
- **Full AG-UI Protocol Compliance**: Implements official AG-UI specification with lifecycle events (RUN_STARTED, RUN_FINISHED, RUN_ERROR)
- **18+ Component Types**: button, text, input, container, form, card, modal, tabs, progress, table, list, alert, dropdown, textarea, checkbox, radio, slider, canvas
- **Real-time State Management**: Bidirectional synchronization with localStorage persistence and cross-tab support
- **Multi-Agent Collaboration**: Agent configuration system with capability-based delegation and shared state
- **Streaming Responses**: TEXT_MESSAGE_START/CONTENT/END event pattern for progressive UI rendering
- **Middleware Translation Layer**: Support for OpenAI Functions, WebSocket, and generic REST protocols

## Backend Implementation
- `python/tools/ag_ui_tool.py`: Main AG-UI tool with streaming and lifecycle events
- `python/helpers/ag_ui_parser.py`: Component specification parser with validation
- `python/helpers/ag_ui_validator.py`: XSS protection and input sanitization
- `python/helpers/ag_ui_state.py`: Bidirectional state synchronization system
- `python/helpers/ag_ui_config.py`: Agent capabilities and multi-agent coordination
- `python/helpers/ag_ui_middleware.py`: Protocol translation for external integrations
- `python/api/ag_ui_*.py`: REST API handlers for component events and state management

## Frontend Implementation
- `webui/js/ag_ui_components.js`: Alpine.js component definitions with event handling
- `webui/css/ag_ui.css`: Comprehensive styling with dark/light theme support
- `webui/js/ag_ui_state.js`: Frontend state management with real-time synchronization
- `webui/js/ag_ui.js`: Core AG-UI utilities and event system

## Extension System
- `python/extensions/ag_ui_components/`: Modular component system for custom UI elements
- Support for runtime component loading and registration

## Security & Validation
- XSS protection with dangerous pattern detection
- Input sanitization for all user content
- CSRF protection on API endpoints
- Component specification validation with detailed error reporting

## Integration Features
- **Agent Zero Native**: Seamless integration with existing tool system
- **OpenAI Functions**: Function call translation to AG-UI components
- **WebSocket Support**: Real-time updates and collaboration
- **State Persistence**: Component state survives page refreshes
- **Multi-Agent Delegation**: Automatic routing to specialist agents based on capabilities

## Documentation
- Comprehensive prompts for tool usage in `prompts/default/agent.system.tool.ag_ui_tool.md`
- Updated tool registry in `prompts/default/agent.system.tools.md`

## Statistics
- 30 files changed
- 8,109 lines added
- Full protocol compliance with https://docs.ag-ui.com/ specifications

This implementation enables Agent Zero to generate rich, interactive user interfaces dynamically while maintaining full compatibility with the existing architecture and adding powerful multi-agent collaboration capabilities.

author: brunoviola
body:
This pull request introduces a new implementation of a k-Nearest Neighbors (k-NN) classification model in the `classificacao_knn.py` file. The script performs 10 iterations of training and testing using a dataset, calculates evaluation metrics, and outputs the average results.

### Key changes:

#### Implementation of k-NN classification:
* Added functionality to load preprocessed datasets from a `.npz` file and split them into training and testing sets for each iteration.
* Implemented a k-NN model using `KNeighborsClassifier` from `scikit-learn`, with `k=3` as the number of neighbors. The model is trained and tested on reshaped image data.

#### Metrics calculation and reporting:
* Calculated evaluation metrics including accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score for each iteration using `scikit-learn`'s metrics module.
* Aggregated and displayed the average metrics across 10 iterations at the end of the script.

author: kwojtasinski
body:
This pull request introduces several changes to enhance functionality, improve documentation, and simplify code. Key updates include adding support for configurations stored in object storage (GCS and S3), integrating `commitizen` for versioning and changelog management, and refactoring file handling to support remote paths. Below is a summary of the most important changes grouped by theme.

### Object Storage Support
* Added support for configurations stored in Google Cloud Storage (GCS) and Amazon S3, including examples in `docs/configuration.md` for using schemas and sinks from object storage.
* Implemented `read_text` in `src/mimicry/filesystem.py` to handle reading files from local paths, S3, and GCS, with helper methods for each storage type.
* Added environment variable warnings for GCS and S3 credentials in `src/mimicry/utils.py`.

### Versioning and Changelog Management
* Added a GitHub Actions workflow (`.github/workflows/bumpversion.yml`) to automate version bumps and changelog creation using `commitizen`.
* Integrated `commitizen` in `.pre-commit-config.yaml` for commit message validation.
* Updated `pyproject.toml` to include `commitizen` and its configuration for changelog management.

### Documentation Enhancements
* Added a changelog (`docs/CHANGELOG.md`) to track feature additions and updates.
* Updated `mkdocs.yml` to include the changelog in the navigation.

### Code Refactoring
* Refactored `src/mimicry/core.py` to use the new `read_text` function for loading configurations. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-6534fa23814361632e1542a8158f94b9a28b50d52c5bf8984b5d386b30c6bdcaL21-R22) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-6534fa23814361632e1542a8158f94b9a28b50d52c5bf8984b5d386b30c6bdcaL35-R36)
* Simplified CLI argument handling in `src/mimicry/cli.py` by changing `Path` arguments to `str` for compatibility with remote paths. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-4c89387ba19c6b143a45449d8cb78bec7649c2295d38da07dcd030c87cd81843L20-R19) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-4c89387ba19c6b143a45449d8cb78bec7649c2295d38da07dcd030c87cd81843L81-R79)
* Removed redundant logging in `src/mimicry/data.py` to streamline the `append_to_sink` function.

### Dependency Updates
* Added `boto3` and `google-cloud-storage` as dependencies in `pyproject.toml` to support object storage integration.
* Added `pre-commit` and updated development dependencies in `pyproject.toml`.

author: neuhalje
body:
Switch from path based key lookup where the caller needs to know the whole path to a search based workflow.

Breaking Changes
------------------

- `auth-source-gopass-construct-query-path` removed: this is now done by searching
- The `user` is taken from the gopass secret, the secret's path, or the passed parameter of the user (in this order). Before it always was the passed in parameter.
- Switching to use `gopass find` may find more secrets. E.g. The query for the user `name` will now also find the users `myname` and `misnamer`

author: flydongwoo
body:
<!-- PR은 최대한 다른 사람이 알아보기 쉽도록 자세히 써주세요. 특히 수도 코드 부분은 더더욱요...!!-->

## 🔗 문제 링크
<!-- 해결한 문제의 링크를 올려주세요. -->
https://www.acmicpc.net/problem/10159

## ✔️ 소요된 시간
<!-- 문제를 해결하는데 소요된 시간을 적어주세요. -->
1시간

## ✨ 수도 코드
<!-- 내가 작성한 코드를 모르는 사람이 봐도 이해할 수 있도록 글로 쉽게 풀어서 설명해주세요. -->
우선, 이 문제는 제가 저번 학기에 수강했던 알고리즘 기말고사 실기 1번 문제에 나온 인접 행렬에 관한 문제입니다.
인접 행렬의 ㅇ만 들어도 경기를 일으킬 만큼 PTSD가 세게 왔었는데요 ㅎㅎ
그 PTSD를 깨보고자 선택한 문제입니다. ~~(권오흠 교수님 미워 흥)~~

우선, 이 문제는 N개의 물건이 있고, M개의 비교 정보가 주어집니다!
그리고, 각 비교는 A>B를 의미합니다!
모든 비교 정보를 바탕으로, 각 물건마다 무게를 비교할 수 없는(모르는) 다른 물건의 개수를 구합니다!

제 코드는
1. 물건의 개수 N과 비교 횟수 M을 입력 받습니다.
2. N개의 물건 간 무게 비교 관계를 저장할 2차원 배열(문제의 인접 행렬입니다!!!!) graph를 만듭니다.
- graph[i][j] = 1이면 "i번 물건이 j번 물건보다 무겁다"는 의미입니다.
- 처음에는 모두 0으로 초기화합니다 (비교 정보가 없으니까요)
3. M개의 비교 정보를 입력받아,각 비교 (a, b)에 대해 graph[a][b] = 1 로 설정합니다.
- 즉, a는 b보다 무겁다는 관계를 저장하는 것이죠
4. 플로이드-워셜 알고리즘을 사용하여 모든 물건 쌍 (i, j)에 대해, 직접 비교하지 않았더라도  "i가 k보다 무겁고, k가 j보다 무거우면 → i는 j보다 무겁다"라는 관계를 추가로 찾아냅니다!
- 이것을 통해 간접 비교 가능한 모든 관계를 전파합니다.
5. 이제 모든 비교 관계가 저장된 상태에서,각 물건 i에 대해 다음을 수행합니다!
- i를 제외한 다른 모든 물건 j에 대해 graph[i][j] == 0이고 graph[j][i] == 0인 경우는  "i와 j의 무게 비교가 불가능하다(모른다)"는 뜻이므로,  이런 j의 개수를 세어 출력합니다.

끝입니다~!

## 📚 새롭게 알게된 내용
<!-- 새롭게 알게된 내용이 있다면 작성 해주시고 출처를 남겨주세요. -->

### **Floyd-Warshall Algorithm**이란?

알고리즘 강의에서 배우셨던 분들은 가볍게 리마인드 하고 가면 좋을 듯 합니다. 
쉽게 말해서, 그래프에서 모든 정점 쌍 간의 최단경로를 구하는 겁니다!
주로 음의 가중치가 있을 수 있는 방향 그래프에서 사용되는데, 음의 사이클이 없는 경우에만 유효합니다!

| 항목           | 설명                                                  |
|----------------|-------------------------------------------------------|
| 알고리즘 이름  | Floyd-Warshall (플로이드-워셜)                        |
| 목적           | 모든 정점 간 최단 거리 구하기 (All-Pairs Shortest Path) |
| 그래프 유형    | 방향 그래프, 음의 가중치 허용, 음의 사이클은 불가     |
| 시간복잡도     | O(N³) (3중 for문 사용)                                |
| 자료구조       | 인접 행렬 (2차원 배열)                                 |

플로이드-워셜 알고리즘은 이 점화식을 반복 적용합니다!
```cpp
dist[i][j] = min(dist[i][j], dist[i][k] + dist[k][j])
```

즉, i에서 j로 가는 최단 거리는 기존의 dist[i][j]와 중간에 k를 거쳐 가는 경로 dist[i][k] + dist[k][j] 중에서 더 짧은 쪽으로 갱신합니다.

### **알고리즘 흐름**

1. 인접 행렬 초기화
- dist[i][j] = 간선의 가중치
- dist[i][i] = 0
- 간선이 없으면 INF로 초기화

2. 3중 for문 수행
```cpp
for (int k = 1; k <= N; k++)     // 경유 노드
    for (int i = 1; i <= N; i++) // 시작 노드
        for (int j = 1; j <= N; j++) // 도착 노드
            dist[i][j] = min(dist[i][j], dist[i][k] + dist[k][j]);
```

3. 출력 또는 후처리

| 항목       | 설명                                                                 |
|------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|

author: lnofs
body:
New Features:

- Calculation of Hyperfine A and B coefficients. 
        -Correction factors are still being normalized and cleaned up for accuracy and ease of use.
- New Lineshape: Combination instrument function and Gaussian - Based on Hey 1996 
- Lineshape options now: Skewed, Lorrentzian, Gaussian, GaussianInstrum
- GaussianInstrum combines a gaussian and a flat instrument broadening.
- All thermal functions can include an ion velocity for doppler shift as well.
- Skewness of lorrentzian can be modified as an input parameter
- Zeemansig_Low - Still in testing, but should calculate the low-field approximation signal strength.
- Added ability for disabling energy sorting through BOOL sortE flag in stateprocess and stateprocess_HFS. This can prevent issues with the energy sorting due to degeneracy at 0 field. Default is False. No issues have so far appeared with excluding the sorting now.
- PlotZFan re-worked to be significantly faster. Can do lowfield approximation as well.
- Added sigma tracking for delta m =-1,0,+1. Detail shown in an example.
- Added read_HFSInput function that reads an input file for calculating HFS constants. Result is a dictionary with the headers as keywords.
- Added an example of how to use my fast spectral line generation to determine a required resolution for a spectrometer to observe a feature.
- Added MultiSpec which allows for the easy combination of two overlapping spectra. In order to work properly, the beginning and end wavelengths must match properly.
       - Spectra combined this way can be manually scaled (See CIII example)
 -  When using HFS Zeeman calculations, PsiHFS boolean flag can be set. This is mainly for testing purposes in how the HFS hamiltonian is treated.

Fixes/Changes:

- Added more documentation and comments.
- Correction with g_I ^\prime vs g_I in hyperfine calculation and Zeeman splitting.
- Sign correction for nuclear Zeeman (typically will be opposite in sign to spin and orbital component.)
- Updated wavelength conversion for vacuum to air based on Morton2000
- Minor tweak to polarization calculation: Remove double counting by no longer looking at the absolute value of the delta_m, but both plus and minus individually.
- General structure changes to the organization of the code into labeled cells.
- Corrected an issue with the wigner int-or-half-int function that caused erronius result due to numpy 2.0
- Normalized outputs between HFS and non-HFS cases for various functions.
- All examples have been cleaned up and new ones have been added. All interesting features of the code should be showcased now.
- Hyperfine energy shift also treated as hamiltonian and has wavefunctions applied onto it. This falls in line with general E' = <a|H|b> perturbation theory and was overlooked.
- All sign related details for spin removed as they were incorrectly included.
- Numerous tweaks to Zeeman_Main to account for the inclusion of hyperfine constants and input flags.
- Gaussian lineshape fixed.
- ConvolSpect has a better reduction based on weighted fraction of max possible contribution.
- Removed extra factors of 10 that caused issues in spectra functions that increased computed resolution. This is now controlled by the specres parameter for the input file. Default is 10 (means 10 data points per given pixel width).
- Changed all names to SpectSplit to match the project name.
- Tons of testing and changes to main zeeman functions and Zeemanfan. 

Known Issues:
Voigt profiles seems to not always work well.
HFS fan plot doesn't always revert to the number of B=0 values that is typically expected. Overall structure looks fine enough tho.
Likely issues with including BHFS still.

## Overview

This PR implements a comprehensive video preview system with manual cut editing capabilities and real-time progress tracking for AI transcription, significantly enhancing the user experience in the Live Video Editor.

## 🚀 Key Features Implemented

### 1. Manual Cut Editing System
- **Editable Time Fields**: Double-click on start/end time labels to enter edit mode
- **Real-time Validation**: Format validation (HH:MM:SS), logical order checking, and duration constraints
- **Visual Feedback**: Clear visual states for normal, editing, and error conditions
- **Save/Cancel Mechanisms**: Multiple ways to save (Enter, click outside, Save button) or cancel (Escape, Reset button)
- **Data Propagation**: Changes immediately reflected across all components and persisted to cache

### 2. Enhanced Video Preview Component
- **Cut-specific Playback**: Automatic seek to cut start time with playback limited to cut duration
- **Frame-accurate Timing**: OpenCV-based video player with precise frame timing
- **Audio Synchronization**: Real-time audio playback synchronized with video using audio cache manager
- **Thumbnail Integration**: Cached thumbnails with automatic regeneration when start times change
- **Visual Timeline**: Interactive timeline with current position indicator

### 3. Real-time Faster-Whisper Progress
- **Audio-based Progress**: Progress tracking based on actual audio duration processed
- **Intelligent Throttling**: Updates every 5 seconds to prevent UI jitter
- **Accurate Percentages**: Real progress calculation using `segment.end / audio_duration`
- **Seamless Integration**: Works with existing progress callback infrastructure

### 4. Enhanced AI Processing Pipeline
- **Intelligent Caching**: Multi-layer cache system for transcriptions and complete cuts
- **Two-phase Analysis**: Separate content analysis and timestamp mapping for better accuracy
- **Robust Validation**: Comprehensive cut validation with automatic duration adjustment
- **Fallback Systems**: Auto-fallback between Whisper and Faster-Whisper models

## 🔧 Technical Implementation

### Core Components Modified:
- **`src/core/whisper_transcriber.py`**: Added real-time progress tracking for Faster-Whisper
- **`src/core/llm_cuts_processor.py`**: Enhanced validation and two-phase processing
- **`src/core/cuts_processor.py`**: Intelligent caching and processing orchestration
- **`src/ui/components/video_preview.py`**: Complete manual editing system with validation
- **`src/ui/components/main_editor.py`**: Enhanced component synchronization

### Key Technical Features:
- **Progress Callbacks**: Real-time progress updates throughout the processing pipeline
- **Audio Caching**: Efficient audio segment management for playback
- **Thumbnail Management**: Automatic thumbnail regeneration and caching
- **State Management**: Robust editing state tracking with original data preservation
- **Component Communication**: Seamless data flow between cuts list and video preview

## 📊 Benefits

1. **Enhanced User Experience**: Intuitive manual editing with real-time feedback
2. **Improved Accuracy**: Real progress tracking instead of estimates
3. **Better Performance**: Intelligent caching reduces processing time
4. **Robust Error Handling**: Comprehensive validation prevents invalid cuts
5. **Seamless Integration**: All components work together seamlessly

## 🧪 Testing

- ✅ Manual cut editing with various time formats
- ✅ Real-time progress tracking with Faster-Whisper
- ✅ Audio/video synchronization during playback
- ✅ Thumbnail regeneration on time changes
- ✅ Cache system with complete cuts and transcriptions
- ✅ Component synchronization between cuts list and preview

## 📚 Documentation

- **`docs/MANUAL_CUT_EDITING_FEATURE.md`**: Complete manual editing feature documentation
- **`docs/FASTER_WHISPER_PROGRESS.md`**: Real-time progress implementation guide
- **`docs/PROGRESO_IMPLEMENTACION_COMPLETA.md`**: Complete implementation summary
- **`.github/copilot-instructions.md`**: Updated project-specific coding patterns

## 🔄 Compatibility

This implementation maintains full backward compatibility with existing features while adding new capabilities. All existing workflows continue to work unchanged.

## 🎯 Next Steps

This PR establishes the foundation for:
- Interactive timeline with drag-and-drop editing
- Advanced export options with quality settings
- Enhanced UI animations and visual feedback
- Additional AI model integrations

**Documentation**: All new features are thoroughly documented with usage examples and technical implementation details.

author: milescranmer
body:
The `var"#self#"` symbol refers to the enclosing innermost function. This PR defines it for callable structs to help make usage symmetric. This was first mentioned in https://github.com/JuliaLang/julia/issues/6733#issuecomment-919730591 (@c42f).

This is independent of #58909, but would help make a potential `@__FUNCTION__` macro more general.

```julia
julia> struct Foo end

julia> (foo::Foo)() = var"#self#";

julia> Foo()()
Foo()

julia> bar() = var"#self#";

julia> bar()
bar (generic function with 1 method)
```

In the current code, `var"#self#"` does not work with callable structs:

```julia
julia> struct Foo end

julia> (foo::Foo)() = var"#self#";

julia> Foo()()
ERROR: UndefVarError: `#self#` not defined in `Main`
```

---

If combined with #58909 we can update the tests to use `@__FUNCTION__` rather than `var"#symbol#"`.

author: bdraco
body:
# What does this implement/fix?

This PR significantly reduces the CPU usage of the LD2450 radar component from 18.5% to 4.0% by implementing several performance optimizations. The component was previously consuming excessive CPU time and generating redundant network traffic by publishing identical sensor values repeatedly.

**Background**: The LD2450 radar sensor (used in devices like Apollo R Pro 1) was flooding networks with redundant updates, publishing the same sensor values multiple times per second even when nothing changed. This caused unnecessary network congestion and excessive CPU usage on the ESP device and contributed to making an already warm device much warmer.

## Key Optimizations

1. **Change Detection**: Implements caching to only publish sensor values when they actually change, eliminating redundant updates
2. **Mathematical Optimizations**: Replaces expensive `pow()` function calls with simple multiplication for distance calculations
3. **String Operation Elimination**: Replaces string-based hex conversion with efficient bitwise operations
4. **Early Throttle Check**: Moves throttling logic before buffer validation to avoid unnecessary processing

## Performance Results

**Before optimizations:**
- CPU usage: 18.5% (11,073ms out of 60,000ms)
- Average processing time: 1.95ms per update
- Update frequency: ~94 updates/second

**After optimizations:**
- CPU usage: 4.0% (2,400ms out of 60,000ms)  
- Average processing time: 0.47ms per update
- Update frequency: ~86 updates/second

**Overall improvement: 78% reduction in CPU usage**

## Types of changes

- [x] Bugfix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [x] Code quality improvements to existing code or addition of tests
- [ ] Other

**Related issue or feature (if applicable):**

- fixes #(issue number if applicable)

**Pull request in [esphome-docs](https://github.com/esphome/esphome-docs) with documentation (if applicable):**

- N/A (no documentation changes required)

## Test Environment

- [ ] ESP32
- [x] ESP32 IDF
- [ ] ESP8266
- [ ] RP2040
- [ ] BK72xx
- [ ] RTL87xx

## Example entry for `config.yaml`:

```yaml
# No configuration changes required - optimizations are internal
ld2450:
  - id: ld2450_radar
    uart_id: ld2450_uart
    throttle: 1000ms

sensor:
  - platform: ld2450
    ld2450_id: ld2450_radar
    target_count:
      name: Presence Target Count
    # ... other sensors
```

## Checklist:
  - [x] The code change is tested and works locally.
  - [ ] Tests have been added to verify that the new code works (under `tests/` folder).

If user exposed functionality or configuration variables are added/changed:
  - [ ] Documentation added/updated in [esphome-docs](https://github.com/esphome/esphome-docs).

## Technical Details

### Change Detection Implementation
- Added cache structures to track previous sensor values
- Only publishes when values differ from cached values
- Uses proper sentinel values that don't conflict with valid sensor ranges

### Mathematical Optimizations
- Replaced `pow(x, 2)` with `x * x` for distance calculations
- Reuses already decoded coordinate values instead of decoding twice

### String Operation Elimination
- Replaced `str_snprintf()` and `std::stoi()` based hex conversion with direct bitwise operations
- Eliminated temporary string allocations in the data processing path

### Code Safety
- All sentinel values are outside the valid sensor data ranges
- No functional changes to sensor behavior
- Maintains backward compatibility

body:
# Add Expression Conversion Functions and Fast Selection Sort for Scored Instances

## Description
This PR adds comprehensive expression conversion functions for instances, scored instances, and instance sets, along with a fast selection sort implementation that converts to expressions for sorting. The changes include:

- **Conversion functions**: `instToExpr`, `exprToInst`, `sInstToExpr`, `exprToSInst`, `sInstSetToExpr`, `exprToSInstSet`
- **List methods**: `List.toExpr` and `List.fromExpr` for converting between lists and expressions
- **Fast sorting**: Uses `selectionSort` with expression conversion for better performance
- **Comparator fixes**: Fixed `cScoreExpr<` and `cScore<` functions to properly handle tie-breaking logic
- **Comprehensive testing**: Added extensive test coverage for all conversion functions

## Motivation and Context
The original implementation used insertion sort directly on scored instance objects, which was slower than the available `selectionSort` function. The new approach converts scored instances to expressions, uses the faster `selectionSort` algorithm, and converts back to objects. This provides better performance while maintaining the same sorting behavior.

The conversion functions enable seamless transformation between MeTTa data structures and expressions, which is essential for the sorting optimization and future extensibility.

## How Has This Been Tested?
- **Unit tests**: Added comprehensive `assertEqual` tests for all conversion functions in `instance-test.metta`
- **List method tests**: Added tests for `List.toExpr` and `List.fromExpr` functionality
- **Round-trip testing**: Verified that converting to expressions and back preserves original structure
- **Sorting tests**: Tested `sortSInst`, `sortDeme`, and `insertSInst` with various input scenarios
- **Comparator tests**: Added tests for `cScoreExpr<` and `cScore<` in `cscore-test.metta`
- **Edge cases**: Tested empty instances, complex instances, and NaN handling

## Types of changes
- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)

## Checklist:
- [x] My code follows the code style of this project.
- [x] I have added tests to cover my changes.
- [x] All new and existing tests passed.

## Key Changes Made:

### Files Modified:
1. **`metta-moses/utilities/list-methods.metta`**
   - Added `List.toExpr` function for converting lists to expressions
   - Added `List.fromExpr` function for converting expressions back to lists
   - Implemented recursive list processing for nested structures
   - Added proper handling of empty lists and single elements

2. **`metta-moses/representation/instance.metta`**
   - Added conversion functions: `instToExpr`, `exprToInst`, `sInstToExpr`, `exprToSInst`
   - Added instance set conversion: `sInstSetToExpr`, `exprToSInstSet`
   - Implemented fast `selectionSort` with `sInstComparator`
   - Fixed sorting to use descending order (best scores first)
   - Uses `List.toExpr` and `List.fromExpr` for instance conversions

3. **`metta-moses/scoring/cscore.metta`**
   - Fixed `cScore<` and `cScoreExpr<` tie-breaking logic
   - Changed from `(> $cl $cr)` to `(< $cl $cr)` for proper complexity comparison
   - Ensured consistency between object-based and expression-based comparators

4. **`metta-moses/representation/tests/instance-test.metta`**
   - Cleaned up old commented tests
   - Added comprehensive `assertEqual` tests for all conversion functions
   - Added round-trip conversion tests
   - Added sorting and comparator tests
   - Added tests for list method integration

5. **`metta-moses/scoring/test/cscore-test.metta`**
   - Added tests for `exprToCScore`, `cScoreExpr<`, and `cScoreToExpr`
   - Added round-trip conversion tests
   - Added consistency tests between `cScoreExpr<` and `cScore<`
   - Used `let*` for better test readability

6. **`metta-moses/utilities/tests/list-methods-test.metta`**
   - Added comprehensive tests for `List.toExpr` and `List.fromExpr`
   - Tested empty lists, single elements, and complex nested lists
   - Added round-trip conversion tests
   - Tested edge cases and error conditions

### Performance Improvements:
- **Faster sorting**: Uses `selectionSort` instead of insertion sort
- **Expression-based operations**: Enables more efficient sorting algorithms
- **List conversion optimization**: Efficient conversion between lists and expressions
- **Maintained functionality**: All existing behavior preserved

### Bug Fixes:
- **Comparator logic**: Fixed tie-breaking in `cScore<` and `cScoreExpr<`
- **Sorting order**: Ensured proper descending order (best scores first)
- **NaN handling**: Proper handling of NaN values in comparisons
- **List conversion**: Fixed recursive list processing for nested structures

### New Features:
- **List expression conversion**: `List.toExpr` and `List.fromExpr` functions
- **Instance expression conversion**: Complete conversion pipeline for instances and scored instances
- **Fast sorting pipeline**: Expression-based sorting with conversion back to objects
- **Comprehensive testing**: Full test coverage for all new functionality

The changes maintain backward compatibility while providing significant performance improvements and better test coverage. The list methods serve as the foundation for the instance conversion functions, enabling the entire expression-based sorting optimization.

This poses a security risk. GitHub's Security Hardening guide recommends pinning actions to full length commit. - [GitHub Security Guide](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions#using-third-party-actions) - [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security Guide](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#pinned-dependencies) ### Harden Runner [Harden-Runner](https://github.com/step-security/harden-runner) is an open-source security agent for the GitHub-hosted runner to prevent software supply chain attacks. It prevents exfiltration of credentials, detects tampering of source code during build, and enables running jobs without `sudo` access. See how popular open-source projects use Harden-Runner [here](https://docs.stepsecurity.io/whos-using-harden-runner).

author: suvarchal
body:
This PR cleans up needless module interfaces for subroutines/procedures outside of module scope. we have files named as modules (or wanna be modules) but have multiple modules as interfaces for dangling subroutines. For instance, see  https://github.com/FESOM/fesom2/blob/2d82154af65293105ab436a17cfbba697900dcdc/src/oce_dyn.F90#L12-L200, each of these interfaces just wrap one subroutine and define types again inside. This is hard to maintain because if subroutine has to be changed for type say to single precision for a array then we also need to modify the interface too. Moreover when these subroutines need to be used else where we have to use use module_interface_sub1, sub2,sub3 ... we could instead just use from module_interface use sub1,sub2, sub3. this is cleaner, maintainable pattern for changing internal code and useful to have external interfaces such as calling these routines from python or other model.  for some parts this is a simpler fix by  wrapping the current module with a module and end module and remove needless interfaces and use the procedures from this module. For instance see change for above oce_dyn.F90 here https://github.com/FESOM/fesom2/blob/70ee9ba7b179821a4148f6e4dcf9985d99352590/src/oce_dyn.F90#L1-L200  and how it is used here https://github.com/FESOM/fesom2/blob/70ee9ba7b179821a4148f6e4dcf9985d99352590/src/oce_ale.F90#L1-L20 

I guess this happened from early on migration from f77 and early f90 compilers  would generate any implicit interface for dangling subroutines (that are outside module, program blocks) but as that practice slowly started getting discouraged because it is source of bugs compilers started to complain of need to have explicit interface for each dangling subroutine and we in time-rush wrote one for each subroutine when and where that compilation error came. 

the benefits are cleaner code on multiple fronts like allows explicitly mentioning what procedures we are going to use,  less boiler plate imports like use mod_mesh, mod_partit that are needed almost in every subroutine now gets just done at the top of module and shared. And for all above reasons it also allows agentic coding/RAG is much easier to figure out what procedure and their data dependency this way. 

this PR reduces total compiled modules of fesom from 177 to 127,  there are still a few contrived hard parts, it is a bit slow process as most of these changes are better done manually and need some care, but once done i believe our code can use super agentic powers :).

body:
## Summary

- Fixed debugger Memory and Disassembler views losing their address position when switching tabs
- Eliminated flickering effect during address navigation
- Resolved window resize causing unwanted state resets

## Problem

Users reported that switching between debugger tabs would reset views back to address `0x0000`, making debugging workflows inefficient. Additionally, there was a flickering effect when changing addresses due to circular state synchronization.

## Solution

1. **Lifted state to parent**: Moved address state from individual components to `DebuggerLayout`
2. **One-way data flow**: Child components notify parent of changes without creating feedback loops
3. **Eliminated circular sync**: Removed bidirectional synchronization that caused flickering
4. **Persistent navigation**: Views now maintain their position across tab switches and window resizes

## Technical Changes

- **DebuggerLayout.tsx**: Added `memoryViewAddress` and `disassemblerAddress` state
- **DisassemblerPaginated.tsx**: Accept `currentAddress` and `onAddressChange` props
- **MemoryViewerPaginated.tsx**: Accept `currentAddress` and `onAddressChange` props
- **user_experience_analysis.md**: Updated to reflect fix completion

## Test Plan

- [x] Switch between Memory and Disassembly tabs - position should persist
- [x] Navigate to different addresses (e.g., 0x0280) and switch tabs - should maintain position
- [x] Resize window while in disassembler - should not reset address
- [x] Use address input field - should not flicker between old and new values

body:
## 🤖 Installing Claude Code GitHub App

This PR adds a GitHub Actions workflow that enables Claude Code integration in our repository.

### What is Claude Code?

[Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code) is an AI coding agent that can help with:
- Bug fixes and improvements  
- Documentation updates
- Implementing new features
- Code reviews and suggestions
- Writing tests
- And more!

### How it works

Once this PR is merged, we'll be able to interact with Claude by mentioning @claude in a pull request or issue comment.
Once the workflow is triggered, Claude will analyze the comment and surrounding context, and execute on the request in a GitHub action.

### Important Notes

- **This workflow won't take effect until this PR is merged**
- **@claude mentions won't work until after the merge is complete**
- The workflow runs automatically whenever Claude is mentioned in PR or issue comments
- Claude gets access to the entire PR or issue context including files, diffs, and previous comments

### Security

- Our Anthropic API key is securely stored as a GitHub Actions secret
- Only users with write access to the repository can trigger the workflow
- All Claude runs are stored in the GitHub Actions run history
- Claude's default tools are limited to reading/writing files and interacting with our repo by creating comments, branches, and commits.
- We can add more allowed tools by adding them to the workflow file like:

```
allowed_tools: Bash(npm install),Bash(npm run build),Bash(npm run lint),Bash(npm run test)

author: copilot
body:
## Overview

This PR addresses the issue of dead comments throughout the `campaign_crafter_api` directory, significantly improving code readability and maintainability by removing **101 lines of redundant, obsolete, and obvious comments** across 27 files.

## What was cleaned up

### 1. Redundant Import Comments
Removed comments that just restate what import statements already show:
```python
# Before
from app import models, orm_models # Added models import, Added orm_models import
import re # Added import

# After  
from app import models, orm_models
import re
```

### 2. Parameter Change Tracking Comments
Eliminated development history comments that add no value:
```python
# Before
async def generate_text(self, prompt: str, current_user: UserModel, db: Session) -> str: # Changed _current_user
    if not await self.is_available(current_user=current_user, db=db): # Pass corrected args

# After
async def generate_text(self, prompt: str, current_user: UserModel, db: Session) -> str:
    if not await self.is_available(current_user=current_user, db=db):
```

### 3. Obvious Inline Comments
Removed comments that just repeat what the code clearly shows:
```python
# Before
if isinstance(block_content, list):
    block_content = "\n".join(map(str, block_content)) # Ensure all elements are strings
processed_content = block_content.strip() # Remove any leading/trailing whitespace

# After
if isinstance(block_content, list):
    block_content = "\n".join(map(str, block_content))
processed_content = block_content.strip()
```

### 4. Commented-Out Debug Code
Removed 48+ instances of commented-out debug prints and unused code blocks:
```python
# Before
# print(f"OpenAI Key loaded: {'Yes' if settings.OPENAI_API_KEY != 'YOUR_OPENAI_API_KEY' else 'No'}")
# print(f"Local LLM Base URL: {settings.LOCAL_LLM_API_BASE_URL}")

# After
# (Removed entirely)
```

### 5. Placeholder Redundancy
Cleaned up comments that just restate "placeholder" when the code already contains it:
```python
# Before
output.append(f"**Armor Class** :: AC placeholder (e.g., 16 (breastplate))") # Placeholder

# After
output.append(f"**Armor Class** :: AC placeholder (e.g., 16 (breastplate))")
```

## What was preserved

- **Error handling explanations** - Comments explaining complex error scenarios
- **Business logic documentation** - Comments explaining "why" not just "what"  
- **Active TODOs** - Legitimate future development tasks
- **Configuration notes** - Important setup and usage information
- **Complex algorithm explanations** - Comments that add real understanding

## Impact

- **Improved readability**: Signal-to-noise ratio in comments significantly improved
- **Easier maintenance**: Less clutter when reviewing and modifying code
- **No functionality changes**: All tests pass, no behavioral changes
- **Better development experience**: Developers can focus on meaningful comments

## Files with significant improvements

- `app/services/export_service.py` - Major cleanup of redundant formatting comments
- `app/services/*.py` - All service files cleaned of import/parameter change comments  
- `app/api/endpoints/*.py` - All endpoint files cleaned of change tracking comments
- `app/core/config.py` - Removed debug print statements
- `app/core/security.py` - Removed commented-out password functions

## Testing

- ✅ All existing functionality preserved
- ✅ Import statements work correctly  
- ✅ Core services load without errors
- ✅ Security tests pass

This cleanup makes the codebase more professional and easier to work with while preserving all valuable documentation.

author: copilot
body:
## Overview

This PR implements a complete file transfer application with QR code integration from QR-Code-Pro, featuring WebRTC P2P functionality and responsive design. The application allows users to create rooms, generate QR codes for easy sharing, and transfer files directly between devices.

## Features Implemented

### 🔗 QR Code Integration (from QR-Code-Pro)
- **Auto-generate QR codes** when creating rooms
- **QR codes contain room participation links** for easy joining
- **Copy QR code to clipboard** functionality
- **Download QR code as PNG** for sharing
- **Responsive QR code display** optimized for mobile devices

### 🏠 Room Management System
- **Create rooms** with optional custom names or auto-generated IDs
- **Real-time room information** display (name, ID, participant count)
- **Copy room link** functionality for easy sharing
- **Join rooms** via QR code scan or direct link input

### 📁 WebRTC P2P File Transfer
- **Direct browser-to-browser** file transfer (no server storage)
- **Drag & drop interface** for intuitive file selection
- **Multiple file support** with real-time progress tracking
- **File transfer history** with status tracking
- **Connection status** display with auto-reconnection

### 📱 Mobile-Responsive Design
- **Mobile-first CSS design** with responsive layouts
- **Touch-friendly interface** optimized for smartphones
- **Adaptive QR code sizing** for different screen sizes
- **Responsive grid layouts** that stack on mobile

## Technical Implementation

### Backend (Node.js + Socket.io)
```javascript
// Room management with WebRTC signaling
const rooms = new Map();
io.on('connection', (socket) => {
  socket.on('create-room', (data) => {
    const room = createRoom(data.name);
    socket.emit('room-created', { room: room.toJSON() });
  });
});
```

### Frontend QR Integration
```javascript
// QR generation integrated from QR-Code-Pro
class QRGenerator {
  generateQR(data, size = 280) {
    // Fallback to QR API for reliable generation
    const qrUrl = `https://api.qrserver.com/v1/create-qr-code/?size=${size}x${size}&data=${encodeURIComponent(data)}`;
    return this.renderQRImage(qrUrl, size);
  }
}
```

### WebRTC P2P File Transfer
```javascript
// Direct peer-to-peer file transfer
const peer = new SimplePeer({ initiator: true });
peer.on('connect', () => {
  // Send file metadata and chunks
  this.sendFileToPeer(fileData, peer);
});
```

## Project Structure

```
quick-file-transfer/
├── public/
│   ├── index.html              # Homepage with room creation
│   ├── room.html               # File transfer room interface  
│   ├── css/style.css           # Responsive CSS styles
│   ├── js/
│   │   ├── app.js              # Homepage functionality
│   │   ├── room.js             # WebRTC file transfer logic
│   │   └── qr-generator.js     # QR code generator (from QR-Code-Pro)
│   └── lib/
│       ├── simple-peer.min.js  # WebRTC P2P library
│       └── qrcode.min.js       # Local QR generation fallback
├── server.js                   # Node.js server with Socket.io signaling
├── package.json               # Dependencies and scripts
└── README.md                  # Complete documentation
```

## Screenshots

**Homepage with Room Creation:**
![Homepage](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b20f3d18-7f2b-4142-b15b-908b93880278)

**Room Created with QR Code:**
![Room with QR Code](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5ecb8bec-3776-4a85-92db-1308fb7f4890)

**File Transfer Interface:**
![File Transfer Room](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/10ef6645-05a4-4c23-9b3d-6f0eb4a589e4)

**Mobile Responsive Design:**
![Mobile View](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6863e0a4-3943-4fc7-b017-cc7b0cc0fbdf)

## Usage

1. **Start the server:**
   ```bash
   npm install
   npm start
   ```

2. **Create and share rooms:**
   - Visit `http://localhost:3000`
   - Click "Tạo phòng" to create a new room
   - QR code is automatically generated
   - Share QR code or room link with others

3. **Transfer files:**
   - Drag & drop files or click to select
   - Files transfer directly P2P via WebRTC
   - Real-time progress tracking

## Key Benefits

- **Privacy & Security**: Files never touch the server, direct P2P transfer
- **Easy Sharing**: QR codes make room joining effortless on mobile
- **Cross-Platform**: Works on any modern browser, any device
- **No Installation**: Pure web application, no apps to download
- **Vietnamese Interface**: Complete localization for Vietnamese users

## Testing

The application has been thoroughly tested with:
- ✅ Room creation and QR code generation
- ✅ Mobile responsive design across different screen sizes  
- ✅ WebRTC signaling and connection establishment
- ✅ File drag & drop functionality
- ✅ Real-time status updates and error handling

This implementation successfully integrates QR-Code-Pro functionality into a production-ready file transfer application, meeting all requirements specified in the original issue.

# Summary

Adds "trust" levels to Lua scripts.

Scripts now run in "untrusted" mode by default, in which they are sandboxed and all calls to unsafe APIs fail.

Scripts can be trusted via a dropdown next to the start button. In addition, script trust is also persisted based on the script path.

List of unsafe APIs:

`os.execute`
`io.popen`
`os.remove`
`os.rename`
